source.title: Sequential replay of nonspatial task states in the human hippocampus.

confidence_rationale: Supplies the half of ARC-031 that the position-coding literature does not: SEQUENCES. Human hippocampal fMRI patterns at rest reflected the sequential structure of previously experienced nonspatial decision-task states, with consecutive patterns corresponding to nearby states -- replay of a trajectory through an abstract state space rather than a static map of it. The correlation with orbitofrontal task-representation fidelity, itself tied to performance, is the additional finding that matters architecturally: it suggests replayed abstract sequences are doing constructive work on representations elsewhere. Held at 0.5 because the sequences replayed are of EXPERIENCED task states, not planned self-state transitions, and because ARC-031 needs prospective trajectory generation, which offline replay of past episodes is related to but is not.
failure_signatures: Replay is retrospective -- sequences of states the participant actually visited during the task. ARC-031 requires PROSPECTIVE generation and evaluation of candidate deliberation sequences ('resolve uncertainty in X, then attend to Y, then commit'). Retrospective replay is a plausible substrate for building the space in which planning would later occur; it is not the planning.

The state space is a decision TASK's state space -- externally defined by the experimenter, learned from feedback. ARC-031's z_self is the agent's own internal epistemic state (D_eff, hypothesis-tag integrity). Task states are not self states, and nothing here shows the hippocampus indexing the agent's own condition as opposed to the environment's.

fMRI replay detection is at the edge of what the method can do; the authors themselves frame establishing feasibility as a contribution. Temporal resolution is far below the electrophysiological replay literature and the inference depends on pattern-classifier assumptions.

MECH-092 (offline replay extended to z_self trajectories) is the REE claim this most directly touches, and ARC-031 lists MECH-092 in depends_on. Governance should note this entry may bear more on that dependency than on ARC-031's own distinguishing content.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Participants underwent fMRI while resting after performing a decision-making task with sequential structure. Hippocampal patterns recorded at rest reflected the sequentiality of previously experienced task states, with consecutive patterns corresponding to nearby states. Hippocampal sequentiality correlated with the fidelity of task representations recorded in orbitofrontal cortex during decision-making, which were themselves related to better task performance. The authors conclude hippocampal replay may be important for building representations of complex abstract tasks elsewhere in the brain.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-031's object is a TRAJECTORY through a non-physical space -- a sequence of state transitions -- not a position in one. The abstract-cognitive-map literature overwhelmingly demonstrates position coding; this is the paper that shows sequences through an abstract, nonspatial state space being generated by human hippocampus offline. In REE terms it evidences that the hippocampal machinery ARC-031 proposes to reuse is capable of producing ordered state sequences in a domain with no spatial content, and -- via the orbitofrontal correlation -- that those sequences feed representation-building elsewhere, which is the functional role ARC-031 assigns to deliberation-trajectory navigation.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Retrospective versus prospective is the gap, and it is not small. Replay here reconstructs sequences of states actually visited; ARC-031 asks for generation and evaluation of candidate future deliberation sequences. The two are architecturally adjacent -- offline replay is a standard route to building the model that planning then searches -- but adjacency is not identity, and reading this entry as evidence that hippocampus plans deliberation would be an over-claim. Second gap: task states are experimenter-defined external states, not the agent's own epistemic condition. Note also that ARC-031 lists MECH-092 (offline replay extended to z_self trajectories) in depends_on, and this entry arguably speaks to MECH-092 more directly than to ARC-031 itself; it is tagged to ARC-031 because the claim's trajectory content is what it evidences, but governance should weigh that. Standing caveat: ARC-031 is phase-locked v4 with zero substrate in ree-v3.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans, resting-state fMRI following a sequentially structured nonspatial decision task; hippocampal pattern sequentiality analysis with orbitofrontal task-representation fidelity as a covariate. Science 2019.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality 0.8: high-profile, methodologically ambitious, and the OFC-fidelity correlation gives it functional traction most replay-detection papers lack -- discounted from higher because fMRI replay detection is near the method's limit and the authors present feasibility itself as part of the contribution. Mapping fidelity 0.45: it delivers the sequence/trajectory half of ARC-031 that no other entry in this pull does, but on experienced rather than planned sequences and on task rather than self states. Transfer risk 0.5: the transferred object is a computational role for offline sequence generation, which travels reasonably well to an artificial architecture.
